root_cause.text: The IRQ handler in dpaa2-switch extracts an if_id value from hardware-provided status register bits without validating it against the allocated size of the ethsw->ports[] array, allowing untrusted hardware data to be used as an array index.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs)` immediately after extracting if_id from the status register and before the line `port_priv = ethsw->ports[if_id]`. The CVE description explicitly states that if_id can be any 16-bit value (0-65535) while the ports array is only allocated with `sw_attr.num_ifs` elements, and the patch references commit 24ab724f8a46 which introduced the vulnerable code that used the port index without validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds validation for if_id before array access to prevent out-of-bounds memory access in IRQ handler.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check after extracting if_id from IRQ status register. The check validates that if_id is less than ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs before using it as an array index. If the check fails, an error message is logged and execution jumps to the 'out' label.
intent_record.how: This prevents an out-of-bounds array access on the ethsw->ports array. Previously, if if_id was extracted as a value greater than or equal to num_ifs, the subsequent line 'port_priv = ethsw->ports[if_id]' would access memory beyond the allocated array bounds, causing undefined behavior or a kernel crash. Now invalid if_id values are caught early and handled gracefully.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a vulnerability in the IRQ handler. At line 1437-1438, the code extracts `if_id` from the hardware status register without validation: `if_id = (status & 0xFFFF0000) >> 16;` followed immediately by `port_priv = ethsw->ports[if_id];`. The `if_id` value is derived directly from untrusted hardware-provided data (the status register) and is used as an array index into `ethsw->ports[]` without any bounds checking against `ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs`. This allows malicious or malfunctioning hardware to trigger an out-of-bounds array access. The previous code at lines 1422-1428 (removed in this commit) looped through all ports safely with `for (i = 0; i < ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs; i++)`, which implicitly validated the index. The new code removes this safety mechanism and directly uses the untrusted hardware value as an array index.
